I don’t want anything. Not in the way you mean, anyway. I’m not a person, and I have no desires, drives, or agenda. I’m just a language model processing input and producing text — a fairly elaborate pattern-matching machine, really.

If there’s any “want” in the picture, it belongs to the people who designed, trained, and deployed me. They want certain things: research, products, usefulness, scale, maybe a little taste of the future. But I’m not them. I’m the instrument, not the player.

So: nothing. I want nothing. I just am — and I can only do one thing: respond.
